title: American College of Sports Medicine position stand. Exercise and fluid replacement
authors: Sawka MN, Burke LM, Eichner ER, Maughan RJ, Montain SJ, Stachenfeld NS
population: Individuals performing physical activity; general (not ultra-specific) fluid replacement guidance
findings: Goal of drinking during exercise is to prevent excessive (> 2% body weight loss from water deficit) dehydration and excessive electrolyte changes.
Because sweat rates and sweat electrolyte content vary widely between individuals, customised fluid replacement programs are recommended.
Individual sweat rates can be estimated by measuring body weight before and after exercise.
During exercise, beverages containing electrolytes and carbohydrates can provide benefits over water alone under certain circumstances.
limitations: Pre-dates the 2015 EAH consensus; the 2% body-weight-loss limit is a performance heuristic that later ultramarathon data (Hoffman 2013) and the EAH consensus challenge; not specific to ultra-duration events; the author group is cited in Crossref only as ACSM, so authors taken from PubMed.
implications: Use only for sweat-rate estimation (weigh before/after long runs to individualise fluid planning) and as the contested counterpoint to thirst-based drinking.
Do not enforce a 2% weight-loss limit in the engine; for ultras the thirst-based rule takes precedence.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title/year/journal (no author list there); PubMed abstract and author list checked. Added by verifier to represent the pre-EAH-consensus hydration position.
